deviations: idea_search.py: deleted the whole inline `class ParturaScorer` + `SCORERS = []` block (design step 5 literally names only lines 168-176 for the make_scorer wrapper and 180-239 for install(arm)) -- kept, it would be dead, duplicate code now that ParturaScorer lives in ac_plugin.py and is reached through the scorer registry; this is clearly implied by ac_plugin.py's own design text ("_partura_scorer_factory ... is today's ParturaScorer"), so I removed it too.

Design step 7 says the guidance's thinning draw should become `u=gen.hook_rng.random()`. Verified against generator.py/gp.py/pipeline.py: SearchHooks.accept is invoked as `self.accept_hook(tree)` (one positional argument, no generator reference -- confirmed by generator.py's own _check_accept_hook docstring), and nothing run_mining/GPMiner/RunResult returns to the caller exposes the TypedTreeGenerator instance (pipeline.py's own `miner_ref` is a local; RunResult has no such field). idea_search.py therefore keeps its own dedicated, seed-reproducible `random.Random(SEED)` (reseeded per arm) instead of touching the live `gen.hook_rng` object -- this satisfies the stated purpose (independent of the tree-building RNG, reproducible from the seed) without reaching an object nothing else in the system reads anyway.

Design step 8 (report `generator.unaccepted_fallbacks` per arm in evidence.json) has the same root cause as the item above and no workaround: it is a genuine instance counter on a component the caller cannot reach through run_mining's public interface. Left unimplemented, with an explanatory code comment rather than a faked substitute metric. Needs a new parameter/return field on alphacube.pipeline.run_mining or mining.gp.GPMiner to fix for real -- that is AlphaCube-steering territory, outside WP11's four owned files.

ac_plugin.search_hooks()'s own code-sample comment in the design says it is "read by cli / idea_search", but scripts/idea_search.py does NOT call it: the script keeps its existing, independently-correct base_weight/EXT/risky computation (which it needs anyway for its own diagnostic print) rather than routing the control/steer op_weight through the plugin function. This is the more conservative, zero-behaviour-change option; the two formulas are intentionally identical. Wiring idea_search.py through search_hooks() instead would be a reasonable, low-risk follow-up.

Design step 10 ("re-run one short idea_search episode ... with --arms steer,control") was not run via the actual scripts/idea_search.py: that script hardcodes device="cuda" in three places and a server-only STORE/MIRROR path, and the host rules forbid connecting to any server. Verified the same property instead with a scratch, CPU-only, synthetic-store stand-in (not committed, left at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/wp11_verify/run_episode_smoke.py per the task's own scratch-directory rule) that exercises the real alphacube.pipeline.run_mining -> GPMiner -> TypedTreeGenerator path with ac_plugin's SearchHooks and the "partura" fitness kind end to end: both arms completed and scored 64 candidates each with no exceptions and no monkeypatching anywhere; the steer arm's sampling counters populated ({'proposed': 192, 'thinned': 128, 'accepted': 64}) while the control arm's stayed empty ({}), i.e. the two arms differed in exactly the intervention.

result.notes:
New public names (for reviewers and whoever implements the next package): partura.ac_plugin.register() / .search_hooks() / .set_scorer_state(ctx, kind, split) / .ParturaScorer(target, warmup, cut, **kw) / ._partura_scorer_factory(target, *, dates=None, warmup=0, **kw) / .SCORERS (a module-level list, same role the old script-local SCORERS had). partura.ops_ext.install_kernels() replaces install() -- it is no longer auto-run at import (only the @op registration and the nine kernels' real_valued flags still happen automatically on import); a caller now has to call it explicitly, which ac_plugin.register() does.

Numeric-equivalence note for the scorer migration: scripts/idea_search.py's one caller always has warmup == 0 (its START is the store's first date, so both its PanelSet's and its run_mining call's lead-in trim are always 0 for the same store/start/warmup) -- in that case ParturaScorer's new [warmup:] slicing is a no-op and _partura_scorer_factory's freshly-computed `cut` is bit-identical to the old script's closed-over `cut`; pinned by test_scorer_factory_warmup_zero_reproduces_the_scripts_own_cut and by the end-to-end scratch run. For a hypothetical warmup > 0 caller the factory slices target and every scored panel by [warmup:] before using them, which is what keeps them aligned with Partura's own ctx (itself built from a PanelSet whose own trim must equal that same warmup, for the same store/start/warmup) -- reasoned from source since there is no second real caller to cross-check this path against.

Things I was not fully sure about and resolved by reading source rather than guessing: whether SearchHooks.accept receives the generator (it does not -- confirmed in generator.py); whether _pick_weighted's face-mass formula matches Partura's old `pick` (it does, by design and by its own docstring, which cites scripts/idea_search.py's old line numbers directly); whether register_scorer tolerates being called more than once per process (it does, for the identical factory object -- confirmed by its own docstring and by a dedicated test). I verified the "9 kernels / 304 registry entries" numbers empirically against an unpatched alphacube.catalog.build_registry() rather than trusting the design doc's prose.

tests/test_ac_plugin.py covers the design's five WP11 test bullets plus: _partura_scorer_factory's dates/warmup validation, a shape+NaN-pattern misalignment guard, score()/score_combined() parity and bookkeeping, op_weight removing a whole operator face, op_weight boosting one operator, SearchHooks differing only in op_weight/accept, PanelSet.view_id's daily-store identity and stability (including the no-daily-source byte-identical-contract_hash backward-compat claim), and a structural smoke check of idea_search.py's source (it cannot be imported or run as a unit test -- it reads sys.argv at import time and its one real caller needs a GPU and a server store).

No files outside the five above were touched; AlphaCube-steering's worktree is untouched (git status empty there, confirmed before and after the Partura-steering test runs). Nothing was pushed.
